function: p. 6: DDPG allocates each UAV's CPU-frequency coefficient and uplink bandwidth to minimize federated learning round latency and energy (aerial-link resource allocation joint with computing).
system: pp. 8-9: UAV-aided IoT, 20 FL clients, 5 MHz total bandwidth, 5e-5 W fixed user power; antenna configuration and carrier frequency not stated; no RIS.
method: pp. 6-7: Deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) actor-critic reinforcement learning at the server; state is battery, CPU frequencies and channel estimates; reward from latency and energy.
data_channel: pp. 3, 8: A2G path loss of [8], no small-scale fading; own Python simulation with random client battery, CPU, data size; no 3GPP model or measured data.
test_conditions: pp. 8-9: DDPG trained and evaluated in the same simulated setting with 20 clients, for lambda 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, up to 1000 episodes; no unseen scenario or transfer tested.
baselines: pp. 8-9: DQN (learned, Fig. 4c); Static, Bandwidth and Energy Factor (EF) allocation methods (Table II); random-start PSO, K-means, iterative deployment (Fig. 3, non-learned part).
metrics: pp. 8-9: Latency (ms), energy (J), maximum FL rounds, reward; for deployment SINR (dB) and data rate (bps/Hz).
q1_support: p. 3: "Small-scale fading effects are disregarded". Path loss only, from the A2G formula of [8]; the Python simulation of SAP (p. 8) names no channel model; no 3GPP TR 38.901 or 38.811 model, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "considering 20 users who have finite battery power". A single configuration; only the weight lambda is varied (p. 9); no test on other numbers of clients, scenarios, or fading is reported.
q3_support: p. 9: "Fig. 4(c) compares the latency achieved by UAV for DDPG and DQN algorithms" (learned baseline) and "has achieved the least latency and energy consumption compared with other conventional methods" (Static, Bandwidth, EF in Table II).
q4_support: p. 2: "A computationally efficient MUECD algorithm" is a qualitative claim about the non-learned PSO deployment. No complexity order, operations, parameters, or runtime is reported for the DDPG (Algorithm 2, p. 7).
q5_support: p. 8: "SAP is extensively simulated using Python". Custom simulation; no link or DOI to code or data, and no public channel dataset, is given.
notes: Borderline eligibility. Only the DDPG of SAP is learned; it allocates CPU frequency and bandwidth to UAV federated-learning clients (p. 6). Deployment (K-means, modified PSO) and SINR-balanced power allocation are non-learned (pp. 4-6). Included under the aerial-link rule of above_phy (learned resource allocation in aerial links, joint with an edge-computing decision) as area 6; FL aggregates digitally (rate from bandwidth and SNR, p. 3), so not area 7. Reviewer to confirm; if bandwidth sharing among FL clients is not read as aerial-link resource control, exclude as above_phy. Transmit power is fixed (p. 8). Table I (p. 8) gives altitude 320-400 m while the text (p. 7) says 10-100 m.
